h.strategy: Propose hypotheses where the condition plausibly changes the edit's effect by a large amount through a simple mechanism: redundancy (an alternative path or component already provides what the edit adds), disconnection (the edited part cannot influence the outcome under the condition), saturation (gains shrink when capacity is already high), or bottleneck (gains grow when the edited part is the limiting factor). Make sure the direction follows unambiguously from the mechanism. Avoid conditions unrelated to the edited part.

hyps.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 receives no input, so edge 2 carries nothing and upgrading it cannot help.
With edge 0 removed node 1 is empty, so edge 4 carries no signal and its upgrade has little effect.
A parallel conv 3x3 path into node 3 already provides learned capacity, so the extra conv on the direct edge is largely redundant.
Node 3 already receives a strong conv 3x3 feature from the direct edge, so another conv on edge 5 adds little.
With edge 4 removed there are fewer learned paths into node 3, so the direct edge is more of a bottleneck and its upgrade gains more.
With edge 5 removed node 2 cannot reach the output, so upgrading edge 1 into it is wasted.
With edge 5 removed node 2 is a dead end, so upgrading edge 2 cannot influence the output.
With edge 4 gone, removing edge 3 leaves only edge 5 into node 3, so the loss of output paths is far more damaging.
A clean skip shortcut into node 3 already supplies a good path, so deepening the 0->1->2->3 chain matters less.
A strong direct conv 3x3 path into node 3 survives, so cutting the 0->1 chain costs less accuracy than when the chain is needed.
